title: Reviewed dispositions recorded for the destructive statements the production schema-upgrade verifier now sees in the forward chain
method: Each statement was re-extracted from supabase/migrations/** with the verifier own normalize (whitespace collapsed, comment lines stripped, split on ";") so every disposition pins the exact text the check compares, rather than text retyped from the DEL-E return. For each one: the whole surrounding region of the migration was read, the migration own comments were read, the object lineage was traced with grep across supabase/migrations/** and against the recovered Production baseline 20260728213131_remote_schema.sql, and re-stated CHECK value lists were diffed set-against-set rather than eyeballed.

dispositionsAdded.reason: the same step replaces this index with two narrower partial unique indexes over the same three columns — one for the actionable statuses, one for applied — so the uniqueness rule is split and relaxed, never removed. Dropping an index removes no row, and a relaxed rule can reject no row that the old index allowed.

ownerDecisionsNeeded.statement: drop policy if exists "consumer wilma telemetry internal safety select" on public.consumer_wilma_telemetry;
ownerDecisionsNeeded.why: This policy exists in the recovered Production baseline (20260728213131_remote_schema.sql line 2598), where it admits any partner_users row with role in (internal_admin, safety_reviewer), with no status and no partner-scope test. The same file recreates it two statements later as `to authenticated using (public.is_internal_admin())`, which is a strict subset: is_internal_admin() requires status = active, role = internal_admin and partner_slug is null. No row is deleted and nothing is widened, but applying this to Production revokes safety-telemetry reads from every safety_reviewer and from any inactive or partner-scoped internal_admin. That is an authorization change on live data, not an idempotency drop. The verifier own later check no_baseline_policy_was_dropped_or_weakened compares baseline policy definitions verbatim and will flag the same change independently, which is a second reason this lane must not sign it off.

ownerDecisionsNeeded.statement: drop policy if exists legalease_os_support_items_internal_admin_all on public.legalease_os_support_items;
ownerDecisionsNeeded.why: Same shape and same baseline (line 2738). The baseline policy grants USING and WITH CHECK for ALL commands to partner_users rows with role in (internal_admin, support_reviewer); the replacement restricts both to public.is_internal_admin() and to the authenticated role. Strictly narrower, loses no row, widens nothing — but it removes an existing support_reviewer class reads AND writes on the support queue, which is an authorization decision on live data reserved to the owner, and it likewise redefines a baseline policy that no_baseline_policy_was_dropped_or_weakened requires to be unchanged.

observationNotBlocking.note: Not a destructive-statement defect and outside this lane writable scope, so it was recorded rather than changed: the drop at line 53 names consumer_pending_screening_results_claimed_matter_id_fkey, but 20260828100000 created its foreign key on the same column as consumer_pending_screening_results_claimed_matter_fkey (no _id_). The drop therefore removes nothing and the chain ends up carrying BOTH foreign keys on claimed_matter_id — the earlier one ON DELETE SET NULL, the new one ON DELETE CASCADE. The migration comment says the SET NULL action was incompatible with the CLAIMED row-shape constraint, so the intent reads as replacement, not coexistence. Worth an owner or author look; it does not affect the disposition, whose only claim is that the drop can remove nothing.

No stale entry was introduced: an independent audit of all 26 destructive statements in the chain against all 24 dispositions (8 pre-existing + 16 added) found 26 matched minus the 2 owner statements, and 0 dispositions matching nothing.

nextBlocker: The two owner decisions above are the immediate blocker on no_unreviewed_destructive_operation. Behind them, the verifier static checks fail fast, so the replay was never reached and could not have run here: scripts/rcap-schema-upgrade-lab.sh requires a PostgreSQL 17 cluster (the baseline grants MAINTAIN, 17+ syntax that cannot replay on 16) and this container has only /usr/lib/postgresql/16/bin. Nothing was installed. This lane therefore makes NO claim that the chain applies cleanly, that the replay is deterministic, or that the upgrade reaches the accepted target schema.
